root_cause.text: The `mmu_set_spte()` function in KVM x86 MMU created MMIO SPTEs before checking and dropping any existing shadow-present SPTE, allowing an MMIO SPTE to be installed on top of a present SPTE and triggering a `WARN_ON` in `mark_mmio_spte()` due to the invariant violation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the MMIO SPTE creation block after the existing shadow-present SPTE handling (the `if (is_shadow_present_pte(*sptep))` block). The commit message explicitly states: "When installing an emulated MMIO SPTE, do so *after* dropping/zapping the existing SPTE (if it's shadow-present)." The warning in the call trace originates from `mark_mmio_spte`, which checks `is_shadow_present_pte(*sptep)`, confirming that a present SPTE was unexpectedly present when marking an MMIO SPTE.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit moves MMIO SPTE creation in mmu_set_spte() to before the check for shadow-present SPTE (lines after pgprintk). If an existing present SPTE is present, calling mark_mmio_spte() will overwrite it via mmu_spte_set(), which triggers a WARN because mmu_spte_set() expects the old SPTE to be not present. This is the vulnerable construct: creating MMIO SPTEs without first dropping the existing present SPTE, as described in the root cause. The fix is not present because the code does not remove the existing present SPTE before writing the MMIO SPTE; it relies on a warning instead of proper handling.
